findings.where: First screen, the contact row: the filled 'Write to me' button and the underlined address Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one personal way to reach Mark does nothing. 'Write to me' is drawn as a filled blue button and the address is underlined like a link, but neither can be clicked (parts map p11–p13: static). A visitor who clicks either one gets no response. The only working mailto link is in the footer, at the very bottom of the page.
findings.who_objects: The bank official who has decided to get in touch. They click the obvious button or the address and nothing opens. They may decide the site is broken or out of date and leave without writing. The brief's personal-advisor test needs one direct way to reach him that works.

findings.where: First screen, the contact row: 'Book a consultation' next to 'Write to me' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: There are two filled buttons of equal weight, with the address between them, so the visitor sees three options and no clear first one. The one button that works, 'Book a consultation', only jumps to an on-page anchor (#consult), and no consultation section appears anywhere on the page. Its wording also sounds like a firm's booking funnel, not a personal advisor.
findings.who_objects: The official has to choose between writing and booking without knowing what 'booking' gets them. Then the button takes them nowhere. A senior MDB official expects to email an advisor, not book a consultation like a retail customer, so the wording feels salesy (brief: one action; 'what fails: salesy').

findings.where: The blue margin notes everywhere: the three hero notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024, with their talk titles) and the section labels (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The notes are set in the house blue, the colour this page uses for links and the action. They look clickable but are not (parts map p5–p10, p15–p26: static). This matters most for the hero notes: they name real talks, and a visitor would expect each one to open the talk or its slides.
findings.who_objects: The official checking Mark's standing clicks 'Best Practices in PPP Legislation for Emerging Economies' to read it, and nothing happens. Either the proof seems to go nowhere, or they learn that blue means nothing on this site, which also weakens the real links.

findings.where: First screen, the paragraph 'I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS, DEVELOPMENT AGENCIES AND GOVERNMENTS…' (desktop four lines; phone eight lines)
findings.fault: The one sentence that says who Mark serves is set in widely spaced capitals over several lines. That makes it the slowest text on the screen to read, and it reads like a corporate label or a tech eyebrow, not his voice. It sits between the large serif heading and the serif paragraph and breaks their tone.
findings.who_objects: The official checking 'is this for me?' has to work hardest on exactly the line that answers it. The founder asked for serious, non-techy type with Mark heard in his own voice, and tracked capitals turn this line into a shouted label.

findings.where: First screen ground: the pale lavender-to-blue gradient behind the hero (desktop and phone), ending in a hard edge onto the warm paper
findings.fault: The hero sits on a cool lilac-blue gradient that is not in the page's own palette, which states 'three colours, no accent' on warm paper. It gives the first screen a soft, slick, app-like tint that the rest of the page never uses, and it stops in a hard line against the paper. On phone it fades out with an empty band of paper below.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for one soft warm ground with the house blue and grey as the only ink. To the visitor, a purple gradient reads more like a tech start-up than a legal advisor.

findings.where: Phone, first screens: the order heading → Istanbul note → photo → caps paragraph → Melbourne note → paragraph → São Paulo note → buttons
findings.fault: At phone width the margin notes fall between the main blocks. They break up Mark's sentences and push the contact action down to the bottom of the second screen. The buttons are also misaligned: 'Book a consultation' is indented from 'Write to me' and the address, and the address is squeezed between the two buttons.
findings.who_objects: An official reading on a phone between meetings has to scroll through stray blue notes before reaching any way to contact Mark, and the uneven button stack looks unfinished.

findings.where: First screen as a whole, and the footer
findings.fault: Apart from talk titles, nothing on the page shows who has hired Mark: no named bank, agency or government, and no role or region of past work. Nothing says where he is based. The navigation has no Contact item. The footer has no year or legal identity.
findings.who_objects: An MDB official who hires through procurement needs to see work done for bodies like theirs before shortlisting him. 'I advise multilateral development banks' is a claim they cannot check. They may move on to an advisor whose page names past mandates.

findings.where: Header: the MMM INFRA lockup at the top left (desktop)
findings.fault: The 'MMM INFRA' lettering under the arches nearly touches the hero band's top edge, with almost no clear space, so the mark looks squeezed into the header bar.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, for whom the mark is the identity. A cramped logo looks careless at the very first glance.

findings.where: Motion sketch section (desktop): the curve on the left and the exhibit photo with its table on the right
findings.fault: The exhibit photo floats at the far right, out of line with the curve. Under the curve the left column leaves a tall empty gap while the table runs on alone, so the section reads as two unrelated pieces.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the tile sees a section that looks unfinished next to the tightly set article specimen above it.

findings.where: First screen and motion sketch: Mark's photograph, set with a soft drop shadow
findings.fault: A static photograph has a lifted shadow, which suggests it floats or can be acted on. The house keeps depth for parts that float or act, and a frame or the paper alone could make it look like an exhibit.
findings.who_objects: Few visitors would notice. A designer holding the house rules would object to the shadow as a borrowed signal on a static image.
